Summary: Scheduler briefing re-fires indefinitely on failure
Description: If conversation.handle() raises an exception, task._last_fired_date is never set and the persistent fact is never stored. The next minute's tick retries, repeating every minute for the entire target hour (up to 60 retries). Wastes API credits.
db._conn.isolation_level = None directly mutates the private _conn attribute of aiosqlite.Connection. If aiosqlite upgrades and changes internals, this silently breaks.

config.py defines scheduler_enabled, morning_briefing_hour, evening_briefing_hour, health_check_interval_minutes, event_subscription_enabled, event_significance_threshold, curator_enabled, fact_min_confidence_prune, webhook_cooldown_seconds, announce_on_events, phone_notify_target, mcp_server_url, mcp_transport — none exposed in config.yaml options.
run.sh exports 8 settings from options.json but skips all autonomous loop settings. Even if added to config.yaml they wouldn't reach the Python process.
Private function (prefixed with _) imported across module boundaries. If signature changes, deprecated wrapper breaks silently.
Same cross-module private import issue as lock.py.

Summary: Redundant import re inside function + _ID_RE compiled every call
Description: re is already imported at module level (line 17). Also _ID_RE = re.compile() is recreated on every function call instead of being a module-level constant.

Summary: Routine names lowercased before storage losing original case
Description: name_norm = name.lower().strip() loses user's original casing. The COLLATE NOCASE on the column already handles case-insensitive lookups without lowercasing.

Summary: Potential TypeError mixing aware/naive datetimes in sort
Description: all_events.sort(key=lambda x: x[0] or _dt.datetime.max) — if x[0] is timezone-aware and datetime.max is naive, Python raises TypeError.

Summary: Fence-stripping fails on malformed AI responses
Description: If AI returns just triple-backtick with no newline or closing fence, produces empty string that fails JSON parsing. Extraction silently returns no facts.

Summary: Rate limiting bypassable via X-Forwarded-For header spoofing
Description: Rate limiter falls back to X-Forwarded-For when request.client is None. Behind a reverse proxy an attacker can spoof this header to bypass rate limits.
Malformed messages caught and logged at warning level with continue. The event is permanently lost with minimal indication.

Summary: Fragile error detection via string prefix
Description: Checks result.startswith('Error') or result.startswith('HA error'). A legitimate HA response starting with 'Error' would be incorrectly flagged as failure.

Summary: delete_event stub registered as tool but returns 'not supported'
Description: If registered via @tool the LLM may try to use it and confuse the user with a 'not yet supported' response.

Summary: CI tests Python 3.12 but production Dockerfile uses 3.13
Description: Not a bug today but if any 3.13-only syntax is used CI won't catch it.

Summary: Directory layout lists old test structure
Description: References tests/test_config.py etc. but actual structure now has tests/unit/ tests/model/ and tests/model_ha/ subdirectories.

Summary: References '423 tests' which is likely outdated
Description: Test count has changed since the recent test directory restructuring.
